verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The first equality is stated symbol for symbol by native_band_path, under the dictionary s = w, Y = H, ChartScales.timeCoefficient h n = c_i, PhysicalGraphBounds.timeDirection = v_t = (√2-1, 1), (coordinates k Y).2 = v(H), gap = Δ; the Lean applies the inverse cover map (coverPower gap).symm to a multiple of v_t rather than the scalar T_g^{-Δ}, which is the same thing by cover_pow_timeDirection, since v_t is an eigenvector with eigenvalue T_g. Two routine steps are needed for the rest. (a) The Lean never names H_0: it is path k H 0, and the second equality is the first at w = 0 together with path_path (path k (path k Y eta) eta' = path k Y eta'), which says every point of the lifted rectangle gives the same path. (b) The r₀ of H_0 is present as a convention in the instantiation, not in the generic lemma: bandGeometry takes an arbitrary center, and ActualSignedGeometry.slotGeometry passes c_γ - r₀·v_t, so (coordinates k Y).2 = λ_t(J_g^Δ Y - c_γ - k_copy + r₀ v_t)/c_i = (η_g(Y) + r₀)/c_i, the paper's v of (6.11), and path k H 0 = H - T_g^{-Δ}(η_g(H)+r₀)v_t as displayed. I checked this by unfolding the definitions (basis = scaledBasis (slotChart vr vt) c_i, coordinates = basis.symm(J_g^Δ Y - center - k)); the same combination (λ_t(·) + r₀)/c_i is written out independently as PhysicalGraphBounds.slotTime, and the pulse window [0, L_s] appears as PartitionedCovariance pulse support Icc 0 (2*radius/c_i). Lean's eta ranges over all of ℝ rather than the paper's w ∈ [0, L_s], which is more general.
